sentences.text: Maraapunisaurus is a sauropod dinosaur whose genus name combines the Southern Ute word for 'huge' with the Greek word for 'reptile'.
The preserved parts of the holotype measured about 1.5 meters in height, while the original height might have reached 2.7 meters.
It possesses the tallest and largest neural spine of any animal, measuring 2.7 meters.
The largest historical estimate placed its length at 58 meters and mass at 150 tonnes.
Even the lowest length estimates for M. fragillimus were higher than those of Supersaurus, Sauroposeidon, and Argentinosaurus.
If recent estimations of Bruhathkayosaurus are accurate, Maraapunisaurus would have been the second largest land animal and the fourth largest animal overall.
Based on Cope's original description, the femur of M. fragillimus was estimated to be 3.6 meters tall.
The species was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1878 during the Bone Wars, a period of intense rivalry between paleontologists Edward Drinker Cope and Othniel Charles Marsh.
The only known specimen was collected by Oramel William Lucas in 1877, and the holotype is a partial vertebra discovered in Garden Park, north of Cañon City, Colorado.
Only one fossil occurrence of Maraapunisaurus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Maraapunisaurus lived in a savanna-like environment similar to those of modern giant herbivores.
Evidence of trees 20 to 30 meters tall has been found in the environment where Maraapunisaurus lived.
Larger animals have longer digestive systems that retain food for longer periods, allowing them to survive on lower-quality food sources.
Researcher Carpenter argued that Maraapunisaurus could consume ferns as a major part of its diet because its digestive system was adapted to process low-quality food.
Carpenter speculated that Maraapunisaurus may have used gallery forests for shade during the day and fed on the open savanna at night.
The species was originally named Amphicoelias fragillimus by Cope in 1878, but was later reclassified as a rebbachisaurid, leading to the creation of the new genus name Maraapunisaurus.
In 2018, Carpenter reclassified the species as a basal member of Rebbachisauridae and renamed it Maraapunisaurus, derived from a Southern Ute word meaning 'huge'.
The basal position of Maraapunisaurus is indicated by the presence of a hyposphene, a trait shared with Histriasaurus, Comahuesaurus, and Demandasaurus.
Maraapunisaurus belongs to the parent group Rebbachisauridae and is classified in the family Rebbachisauridae.
Maraapunisaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period.
Maraapunisaurus lived during the Tithonian stage, from 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.

If Maraapunisaurus is a rebbachisaurid, it would be the oldest known member of that group and the only one discovered from the Jurassic period, and it would be the only known rebbachisaurid discovered from North America.

Kenneth Carpenter proposed a scenario for the disappearance of the specimen in 2006, yet attempts to relocate the quarry using ground-penetrating radar failed because the bones had the same density as the surrounding rock.

Some researchers argue that the size of the Maraapunisaurus vertebra has been overestimated and that earlier scientists accepted the measurements without sufficient skepticism, while a hypothesis suggests that the reported measurement of 1500 mm for the vertebra is a typographical error for 1050 mm.
Size estimates of M. fragillimus must be treated with caution due to the lack of specimens and detailed documentation.

There is a debate regarding the diet of sauropods: Engelmann et al. (2004) dismissed ferns as a food source due to low caloric content, while Carpenter argued that their digestive systems allowed them to consume ferns as a major part of their diet.
